title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: The US has told ships to avoid any Hormuz transit they do not need, and Brent is back above $116, so the Gulf sea lane is getting harder, not easier, before the 3 November US midterms. On the Saudi side, flydubai and Emirates are due to restart some KSA flights from tomorrow, but Jeddah and Red Sea ports are full and the road to Riyadh is jammed ahead of the pre-Ramadan import peak.

stories.headline: US tells ships to avoid unnecessary Hormuz transits
body: The US Navy's Central Command told vessels with no need to cross the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz to stay away. Ships that must go were told to allow extra time, because of heavy traffic and blockade enforcement. Neutral ships may be questioned, boarded or searched. The last similar notice came in mid-July.

Iranian state media says tanker traffic could resume within four to five days if the US lifts its blockade. War-risk cover is reported at 6–10% of hull value per transit, against 0.15–0.25% before the war.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: Washington is now warning ships off, not just Iran. Expect longer and costlier Gulf sea transits; keep Gulf sea surcharges indexed and steer urgent cargo to east-coast ports.

stories.headline: Saudi Red Sea ports brace for a pre-Ramadan import surge
body: Red Sea ports are at capacity and ships can wait days or weeks outside. Jeddah imports rose 94% in August to SAR33.5 billion, and Jeddah now handles 47% of Saudi imports, up from 22%. Imports usually peak before Ramadan, which starts on 8 February.

There is no freight rail from Jeddah to Riyadh. Folk Maritime's CEO describes trucks to Riyadh as 'bumper to bumper'. DHL Global Forwarding's regional CEO says the ports are 'heavily under pressure'. A Neom container terminal is due to open next month.
stories.soWhat: KSA land legs will get slower and dearer into the new year. Price Jeddah–Riyadh trucking and UAE–KSA road for congestion now, and sell guaranteed road capacity before the peak.

stories.headline: Khorfakkan heads for 5 million TEU as Gulf boxes move east
body: Gulftainer says Khorfakkan should reach 5 million TEU of capacity by the end of October, or about 100,000 TEU a week, up from a current limit of 65,000. It plans a $2 billion expansion to 10 million TEU. Weekly throughput already rose from about 8,000 TEU after a new gate complex opened.
stories.soWhat: More east-coast capacity means fewer delays for UAE imports that skip Hormuz. Re-check our Khorfakkan trucking rates and transit times for key importers.

stories.headline: First UAE flights back to Saudi due from 30 October
body: flydubai plans to resume two daily Riyadh flights, four daily Dammam flights and Abha from 30 October. Emirates plans to restart Jeddah on 30 October and Riyadh and Dammam on 8 November. Etihad stays off Riyadh and Dammam until 5 November.

On 28 October, Emirates, Etihad, Air Arabia and flynas flights to Saudi were still cancelled. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted five ballistic missiles and four drones, with debris damaging buildings in Riyadh.
stories.soWhat: New: restart dates for UAE carriers, starting tomorrow. Belly space into KSA may return in steps, but plans can slip; keep road as default and add air only once flights actually operate.

stories.headline: Dubai warehouse rents up 12.4% as tenants stay put
body: Warehouse renewals hit a record of about 8,200 in the first half, up 21.6%, while new contracts fell 51.8%. Dubai rents rose a further 12.4%. Only about a fifth of Dubai's stock is Grade A.
In the Northern Emirates, more than 10 million sq ft opened in the first half, including 5.2 million in Umm Al Quwain, and rents fell 18.5%.
stories.soWhat: Our Dubai storage is worth more at renewal. Hold contract logistics rates in Dubai and offer cheaper Northern Emirates space to price-sensitive clients.

competitors.name: Noatum Logistics (AD Ports)
competitors.headline: Doubles its GCC truck fleet to more than 850
body: AD Ports' logistics arm has doubled its fleet over six months, mostly owned and operated, with GPS on every truck and a central control tower. It sells in-house cross-border road transport and runs a rail shuttle between Khalifa Port and Fujairah Terminals.
competitors.soWhat: A port-backed rival is building its own road network just as KSA road demand peaks. Lock key freight accounts into UAE–KSA road contracts before Noatum prices them.

competitors.name: flydubai Cargo
competitors.headline: Expands 737 freighter network from Dubai World Central for winter
body: From 25 October, flydubai Cargo flies 737-800 freighters to 17 points, including Karachi four times a week, Erbil and Kuwait three times, and Delhi, Almaty, Nairobi and Doha twice. Bishkek and Damascus start in November.
competitors.soWhat: More regional freighter space out of DWC. Use it as a buy option for our Gulf, South Asia and East Africa consolidations.

competitors.name: DSV
competitors.headline: Q3 air yields up 8% on lower volume; Middle East keeps capacity tight
body: DSV's air gross profit per tonne rose 8% while volumes fell 3% to 561,000 tonnes. Group EBIT before special items rose 19.5%. It said the Middle East conflict kept air capacity tight.
competitors.soWhat: Big forwarders are earning on yield, not volume. Support holding our airfreight margins rather than cutting rates.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: Middle East demand surcharge stays in force
body: FedEx's demand surcharge on parcels and freight to and from the Middle East, North Africa, India and Sub-Saharan Africa, reinstated on 21 September, stays 'until further notice'. An extra surcharge on oversized shipments runs to 7 February 2027.
competitors.soWhat: Integrators are keeping regional surcharges on. Our own surcharges are defensible; check we are not cheaper than we need to be on oversize.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Latest result: record Q2 revenue of Dh1.83 billion
body: Revenue rose 22% to Dh1.83 billion in Q2 2026. Net profit was Dh47 million, about seven times a year earlier, and the EBITDA margin rose to 9.9%. Q3 results are not yet out.
competitors.soWhat: Freight drove the record. Protect freight and road margins as port-backed rivals like Noatum add capacity.

opportunities.title: Pre-Ramadan KSA road peak
opportunities.text: Saudi imports peak before Ramadan on 8 February and Jeddah is full. Sell guaranteed UAE–KSA road capacity now.

opportunities.title: KSA air restarts
opportunities.text: flydubai and Emirates plan Saudi restarts from 30 October. Be ready to offer air into Riyadh and Dammam as soon as flights operate.

opportunities.title: East-coast gateway
opportunities.text: Khorfakkan is heading for 5 million TEU. Package east-coast port plus trucking for importers avoiding Hormuz.

opportunities.title: Northern Emirates storage
opportunities.text: Rents there fell 18.5% while Dubai rose 12.4%. Offer cheaper storage options to cost-sensitive clients.

opportunities.title: Regional freighter buy
opportunities.text: flydubai Cargo adds 737 freighter routes from DWC. More options for our South Asia and East Africa consolidations.

watchouts.title: US warning on Hormuz
watchouts.text: Ships may be stopped and searched. Gulf sea transits get longer, and the 3 November midterms are a risk date.

watchouts.title: Brent above $116
watchouts.text: UAE November fuel prices are due around 31 October and are likely to stay high.

watchouts.title: Saudi road congestion
watchouts.text: Trucks to Riyadh are bumper to bumper. Transit times and driver costs into KSA could rise.

watchouts.title: Restart dates could slip
watchouts.text: Missiles were still intercepted over Riyadh on 28 October. Do not promise KSA air until flights operate.

watchouts.title: Port-backed road rival
watchouts.text: Noatum now runs 850+ trucks with cross-border service. Expect bundled port and road offers.

moves.title: Add a congestion clause to KSA road rates
moves.text: Jeddah and the Riyadh road are jammed and the pre-Ramadan peak is coming. Quote KSA road with a waiting-time or congestion charge.

moves.title: Sign KSA road capacity deals before the peak
moves.text: Call top freight accounts this week and offer fixed UAE–KSA road capacity to February, before Noatum does.

moves.title: Prepare a KSA air restart offer
moves.text: Have Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah express rates ready, but switch them on only when flydubai and Emirates flights actually operate.

moves.title: Keep Gulf sea surcharges indexed
moves.text: War-risk cover is 6–10% of hull value per transit and the US now warns ships off Hormuz. Do not fix sea rates past November.

moves.title: Price Dubai storage renewals up
moves.text: Dubai warehouse rents rose 12.4%. Reflect this at renewal and offer Northern Emirates space as the lower-cost choice.

moves.title: Have the November diesel update ready
moves.text: Move road fuel surcharges the day UAE November prices come out, around 31 October.
